sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Technology firmly anchors market leadership with a dominant 0.950 momentum score, while broader market breadth remains narrow with only 2 of 11 sectors showing positive returns across all timeframes.

Leadership continues to concentrate in Technology and Healthcare, with Technology standing out as the lone sustained leader across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons. Meanwhile, Communication Services maintains all-green multi-timeframe status despite a lower YTD rank of 9.

Defensive and rate-sensitive pockets remain pressured at the bottom of the momentum curve. Utilities and Real Estate lag significantly, even as Consumer Defensive managed a modest one-spot gain over the past five sessions to move past Financials.

## Strength
- Only 2 of 11 sectors achieve all-green status across week, month, quarter, half, and YTD: Technology (0.95 momentum) and Communication Services (0.65 momentum).
- Technology is the sole sector demonstrating sustained strength, maintaining a top-3 rank across the 1-, 3-, and 6-month windows with a sector-topping 0.950 momentum score.
- Energy holds the #1 YTD rank with solid momentum of 0.667, joined by Healthcare at a 0.733 momentum score.

## Movers & Momentum
- Consumer Defensive was the sole positive mover over the last 5 sessions, gaining +1 spot to reach rank 6 (momentum 0.417).
- Financials posted the only 5-session rank decline, dropping -1 spot to rank 7 (momentum 0.483).
- Momentum remains heavily skewed to the bottom for Utilities (0.033, rank 10), Real Estate (0.233, rank 8), and Consumer Cyclical (0.250, rank 11).

## Divergences
- Communication Services shows positive returns across all timeframes and a 0.650 momentum score, yet languishes at rank 9 on a YTD basis.
- Energy holds the top YTD rank (rank 1) but trails both Technology (0.950) and Healthcare (0.733) in absolute momentum at 0.667.

- OUT: Energy -> IN: Communication Services - reflecting flow away from deeply negative relative strength (Energy rs_slope -1.069, wk -2.9%) toward positive short-horizon momentum (Communication Services regime +0.27, wk +1.6%, mo +3.3%).
- OUT: Basic Materials -> IN: Consumer Cyclical - moving away from steep medium-term contraction (Basic Materials mo -7.9%, rs_slope -1.460) into stabilizing cyclical exposure (Consumer Cyclical regime +0.17, rs_slope -0.418).

risk_radar.relative_strength: Technology is the sole sector genuinely outperforming the S&P 500, posting an rs_score of 1.00, an rs_confirmed of 1.00, and beating SPY across 7/7 timeframes, while no RS new highs or crosses are reported. The remaining sectors trail significantly, with Communication Services and Energy both lagging at an rs_score of 0.50, an rs_confirmed of 0.17, and beating SPY on only 3/7 timeframes.
risk_radar.risks:
- Extreme concentration risk is evident with leadership crowded into a single sector, Technology (rs_score 1.00, rs_confirmed 1.00, beating SPY on 7/7 timeframes), while all other sectors lag benchmark performance.
- Both Communication Services and Energy display fragile relative strength profiles, where an rs_score of 0.50 (beating SPY on 3/7 timeframes) drops to an rs_confirmed of just 0.17 due to weak directional consistency.
- Severe broad underperformance persists in Consumer Cyclical (rs_score 0.00, rs_confirmed 0.00, beats SPY on 0/7 timeframes) and Healthcare (rs_score 0.17, rs_confirmed 0.17, beats SPY on 1/7 timeframes), leaving market breadth sharply compromised.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** High-momentum technology and healthcare groups remain firmly in control, but market breadth is narrow with only 8 of 144 industries holding all-green status.

Tech and health-related leaders continue to dominate market strength, led by Semiconductors (0.94 momentum), Computer Hardware (0.94), and Diagnostics & Research (0.92). Diagnostics & Research is demonstrating rare dual strength, pairing an elite momentum profile with a rapid 14-spot rank advance over the past five sessions to reach rank 31.

Rotation is surfacing in deeply lagged pockets like Airlines and Real Estate - Diversified (both climbing 20 spots), while cyclical and defensive groups are fading. Logistics and materials are leading the retreat, with Integrated Freight & Logistics dropping 18 spots to rank 69 and Paper & Paper Products declining 16 spots to rank 111. 

## Strength
- **Narrow all-green breadth:** Only 8 of 144 industry groups are positive across week, month, quarter, half, and YTD periods, heavily concentrated in tech and healthcare.
- **Top momentum leaders:** Semiconductors (0.944 momentum, rank 7 YTD), Computer Hardware (0.942 momentum, rank 1 YTD), and Electronics & Computer Distribution (0.939 momentum, rank 3 YTD) maintain the highest momentum profiles.
- **Sustained multi-horizon strength:** Tech giants are joined by Diagnostics & Research (0.92 momentum) and Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing among the sustained leaders keeping top-36 ranks across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Biggest 5-day gainers:** Airlines (+20 spots to rank 84, 0.64 momentum) and Real Estate - Diversified (+20 spots to rank 85, 0.65 momentum) drove the sharpest short-term rank rebounds.
- **Fastest decliners:** Integrated Freight & Logistics shed 18 spots (falling to rank 69, 0.34 momentum), followed by Paper & Paper Products (-16 spots to rank 111, 0.40 momentum) and Agricultural Inputs (-14 spots to rank 39, 0.46 momentum).
- **Persistent laggards:** Bottom-tier momentum remains anchored by Solar (0.059 momentum, rank 137 YTD), Gambling (0.073 momentum, rank 143 YTD), and Personal Services (0.082 momentum, rank 138 YTD).

## Divergences
- **Momentum fading:** Stronger groups seeing short-term distribution include Banks - Diversified (0.73 momentum, -2 spots in 5d), Silver (0.68 momentum, -2 spots in 5d), and Insurance - Life (0.67 momentum, -3 spots in 5d).
- **Emerging early turnarounds:** Rank is rebounding ahead of overall momentum in beaten-down consumer and construction segments, led by Apparel Retail (+11 spots in 5d, 0.44 momentum) and Residential Construction (+11 spots in 5d, 0.40 momentum).
